ai_sections.title: Transformer Losses and Efficiency
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Q6 · practical transformer: equivalent circuit, efficiency and regulation (10M)
paragraphs: A transformer has no mechanical rotation, so the important losses for this unit are winding copper loss and iron/core loss.
Copper loss changes with load current, whereas the iron loss is treated as approximately constant when the applied voltage and frequency are constant.
bullets: Primary copper loss: \(I_1^2R_1\). Secondary copper loss: \(I_2^2R_2\).
At \(x\) per-unit load, copper loss = \(x^2\) × full-load copper loss.
Iron loss consists of hysteresis loss and eddy-current loss.
Output power = input power − total losses.
derivation: Using equivalent resistance referred to the primary, total copper loss may be written as \(I_1^2R_{01}\).
For input power \(P_{in}=V_1I_1\cos\phi\), output is \(P_{out}=V_1I_1\cos\phi-(I_1^2R_{01}+W_i)\).
Therefore \(\eta=P_{out}/P_{in}\times100\).
Differentiating the efficiency expression with respect to load current gives the maximum-efficiency condition \(I_1^2R_{01}=W_i\): variable copper loss equals constant iron loss.
ai_sections.key_point: For efficiency questions, first separate the load-dependent copper loss from the nearly constant iron loss.

ai_sections.title: Basic Construction of a DC Machine
paragraphs: A DC generator and a DC motor use the same basic machine construction. The direction of energy conversion changes, but the main parts remain the same.
bullets: Yoke: outer frame; gives mechanical support and provides a return path for magnetic flux.
Pole cores and pole shoes: carry and spread the main magnetic flux and support the field coils.
Field windings: DC-excited windings that produce the main magnetic field.
Armature core: laminated rotating iron core with slots for armature conductors.
Armature winding: interconnected conductors in which emf is induced and current flows.
Commutator: segmented rotating switching arrangement connected to the armature winding.
Brushes: stationary carbon/graphite contacts that connect the rotating commutator to the external circuit.

formulae.label: Parallel paths
formulae.latex: A=P\text{ for lap winding},\qquad A=2\text{ for wave winding}

diagrams.title: Basic construction of a DC machine
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.31 · Basic construction of a DC machine · Textbook p. 163

ai_sections.key_point: Remember the machine in two groups: field system (yoke, poles, field coils) and armature system (armature, commutator, brushes).

ai_sections.title: DC Generator Principle and EMF Equation
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Q5(b) · derive the DC-generator EMF equation (5M)
2023–24 Q6(a) · generator EMF derivation (5M)
paragraphs: A DC generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction. When armature conductors move through the magnetic field and cut flux, an emf is induced; Fleming’s right-hand rule gives the induced-current direction.

The emf in a rotating coil is alternating internally. The split-ring commutator reverses the coil connection to the external circuit every half-turn so that the current delivered at the terminals is unidirectional.
derivation: Let \(P\) = number of poles, \(\Phi\) = flux per pole, \(Z\) = total armature conductors, \(N\) = speed in rpm, and \(A\) = number of parallel paths.
Flux cut by one conductor in one revolution = \(P\Phi\) Wb.
Time for one revolution = \(60/N\) s.
Average emf induced in one conductor = \(P\Phi/(60/N)=P\Phi N/60\) V.
Conductors in series in each parallel path = \(Z/A\). Multiplying gives the generated emf.

diagrams.title: Simple loop generator
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.26 · Simple loop generator · Textbook p. 161

diagrams.title: Conductor passing through a pole pitch
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.35 · Conductor passing through a pole pitch · Textbook p. 166

ai_sections.key_point: The derivation is simply Faraday’s law applied to one conductor, then multiplied by the number of series conductors in one parallel path.

ai_sections.title: DC Motor Principle and Back EMF
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Part A(c) · significance of back EMF (2M)
2023–24 Q6(b) · working of a DC motor with diagram (5M)
paragraphs: A DC motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force; forces on opposite armature conductors form a torque and rotate the armature.
As the armature rotates, its conductors also cut flux and generate an emf. By Lenz’s law this generated emf opposes the applied voltage and is therefore called back emf \(E_b\).
bullets: Fleming’s left-hand rule gives the force direction in motor operation.
At starting, \(N=0\), so \(E_b=0\); the armature current would therefore be very large if it were not limited by the armature circuit.
As speed rises, \(E_b\) rises and automatically limits armature current.
If mechanical load increases, speed tends to fall; \(E_b\) falls, armature current rises and the developed torque increases. This gives the motor a natural load-response mechanism.

diagrams.title: Back EMF in a DC motor
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.44 · Back EMF in a DC motor · Textbook p. 173

ai_sections.key_point: Back emf is essential: it opposes the supply and controls the armature current as motor speed and load change.

ai_sections.title: Load Characteristics of a Separately Excited DC Motor
paragraphs: In a separately excited DC motor, the field winding has an independent supply, so the field current and flux can be held approximately constant while armature load changes.
bullets: Torque–armature current: with constant flux, \(T\propto I_a\); the characteristic is approximately a straight line.
Speed–armature current: as \(I_a\) increases, the \(I_aR_a\) drop increases, so speed falls slightly.
Speed–torque: because torque is proportional to \(I_a\), the speed–torque curve has the same gentle falling trend.
This gives nearly constant-speed operation over the normal load range.

formulae.label: Torque
formulae.latex: T\propto\Phi I_a\;\Rightarrow\;T\propto I_a\text{ when }\Phi\text{ is constant}

diagrams.title: Torque vs armature-current characteristic
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.52 · Torque vs armature-current characteristic · Textbook p. 179

diagrams.title: Speed vs armature-current characteristic
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.53 · Speed vs armature-current characteristic · Textbook p. 180

diagrams.title: Speed vs torque characteristic
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.54 · Speed vs torque characteristic · Textbook p. 180

ai_sections.key_point: With separate excitation and nearly constant flux, torque follows armature current while speed changes only slightly with load.

ai_sections.title: Speed Control of a Separately Excited DC Motor
pyq_focus: 2023–24 Part A(c) · list DC-motor speed-control techniques (2M)
paragraphs: The motor speed relation shows two basic control routes: change the field flux or change the effective armature voltage.
bullets: Field control: keep armature supply voltage constant and vary the field current with a field rheostat. Reducing field current reduces flux and increases speed; this is used for speeds above rated speed.
Armature control: keep field current approximately constant and vary the effective armature voltage. Lower armature voltage gives lower speed; this is used for speeds below rated speed.
Do not allow the field circuit to open while the motor is running; very weak flux can drive the speed dangerously high.

diagrams.title: Field-control method
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.56 · Field-control method · Textbook p. 182

diagrams.title: Armature-control method
diagrams.alt: Figure 3.58 · Armature-control method · Textbook p. 183

ai_sections.key_point: Field control → above rated speed. Armature-voltage control → below rated speed.

ai_sections.title: Swinburne’s Test
paragraphs: Swinburne’s test is treated here as the R25 no-load test sequence used to estimate the efficiency of a DC shunt machine from no-load measurements.
bullets: Run the machine at rated voltage and rated speed under no-load condition.
Record the no-load line current \(I_{L0}\), field current \(I_f\), input power/voltage as required, and armature resistance \(R_a\).
Find no-load armature current, then subtract the no-load armature copper loss from the no-load input to obtain the constant-loss quantity used in the efficiency calculation.
For the required motor or generator load, add the corresponding armature copper loss to the constant loss and calculate efficiency.
ai_sections.key_point: The test separates the no-load input into armature copper loss and a constant-loss component, then uses those losses to estimate efficiency at load.

ai_sections.title: Three-phase Induction Motor — Types and Construction
pyq_focus: 2023–24 Q7(b) · squirrel-cage vs slip-ring induction motor (5M)
paragraphs: A three-phase induction motor has two main parts: a stationary stator and a rotating rotor. The stator carries a three-phase distributed winding; rotor current is induced rather than supplied directly in normal induction-motor operation.
bullets: Stator: laminated core with slots carrying the three-phase stator winding.
Phase-wound / slip-ring rotor: three-phase rotor winding connected to slip rings and brushes. External resistance can be inserted to reduce starting current and improve starting torque.
Squirrel-cage rotor: conducting bars placed in rotor slots and short-circuited by end rings. The construction is simple and rugged, and no external rotor resistance can be inserted.

rows: Three-phase insulated winding connected to slip rings
Can be inserted through slip rings
Starting current/torque can be improved with external resistance
More complex because of brushes and slip rings

diagrams.title: Phase-wound rotor
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.2 · Phase-wound rotor · Textbook p. 187

diagrams.title: Squirrel-cage rotor
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.4 · Squirrel-cage rotor · Textbook p. 188

ai_sections.key_point: The R25 “types” are distinguished mainly by rotor construction: slip-ring (wound rotor) and squirrel-cage.

ai_sections.title: Induction Motor Principle, Synchronous Speed and Slip
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Part A(d) · define slip and slip speed (2M)
2025–26 Q7(a) · principle of operation (5M)
2023–24 Q7(a) · principle of operation (5M)
paragraphs: A balanced three-phase supply to the stator produces a rotating magnetic field (RMF). The RMF rotates at synchronous speed. Because the rotor has relative motion with respect to this field, emf and current are induced in the rotor and their interaction with the stator field produces torque.
bullets: The rotor turns in the same direction as the rotating magnetic field.
The rotor cannot reach synchronous speed in motoring operation: at \(N=N_s\), relative speed becomes zero, rotor emf/current become zero, and torque disappears.
Slip speed is the speed difference \(N_s-N\). Slip is this difference expressed as a fraction of synchronous speed.
At standstill \(s=1\); at synchronous speed \(s=0\). Rotor-current frequency is \(f_r=sf\).

diagrams.title: Production of rotating magnetic field
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.6 · Production of rotating magnetic field · Textbook p. 189

ai_sections.key_point: Induction requires relative motion. Non-zero slip is therefore necessary for an induction motor to develop torque.

ai_sections.title: Torque–Slip Characteristics
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Q7(b) · torque–slip characteristics (5M)
paragraphs: The torque changes with slip because rotor emf, rotor frequency and rotor reactance all depend on slip. The characteristic has three important regions/points.
bullets: Low-slip region: \(sX_2\ll R_2\), so \(T\propto s\). Torque rises approximately linearly with slip.
Maximum torque occurs when \(s=R_2/X_2\).
High-slip region: \(sX_2\gg R_2\), so \(T\propto1/s\). Torque falls as slip increases further.
At starting, \(s=1\). At synchronous speed, \(s=0\) and torque is zero.

diagrams.title: Torque-slip characteristics
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.9 · Torque-slip characteristics · Textbook p. 196

ai_sections.key_point: For the exam sketch, mark \(s=0\), maximum torque, and the starting point \(s=1\), and label the low-slip and high-slip trends.

ai_sections.title: Synchronous Generator — Working Principle
paragraphs: A synchronous generator (alternator) converts mechanical power into AC electrical power by electromagnetic induction. In the construction used here, the DC-excited field is on the rotor and the armature winding is on the stator.
A prime mover rotates the rotor field. North and South poles sweep past the stationary armature conductors, so the flux linking them alternates and a sinusoidal emf is induced.
bullets: Direction of induced current is obtained using Fleming’s right-hand rule.
With \(P\) poles, one mechanical revolution corresponds to \(P/2\) electrical cycles.

diagrams.title: Cross-sectional view of synchronous machine
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.11 · Cross-sectional view of synchronous machine · Textbook p. 198

ai_sections.key_point: Mechanical rotation of a DC-excited rotor field produces alternating emf in the stationary armature winding.

ai_sections.title: Voltage Regulation by Synchronous Impedance Method
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Q8 · synchronous-impedance method for alternator voltage regulation (10M)
paragraphs: Voltage regulation compares the internal/no-load generated emf required for a stated load with the terminal voltage. The synchronous-impedance (EMF) method obtains the machine impedance from open-circuit and short-circuit characteristics.
derivation: Run the alternator at rated speed on open circuit. Vary field current and plot terminal/open-circuit voltage against field current to obtain the OCC.
Run the alternator at rated speed with the armature terminals symmetrically short-circuited. Vary field current and plot short-circuit current against field current to obtain the SCC.
For the same field current, read \(V_{OC}\) and \(I_{SC}\). Use consistent per-phase values and calculate \(Z_s=V_{OC}/I_{SC}\).
With measured armature resistance \(R_a\), calculate \(X_s=\sqrt{Z_s^2-R_a^2}\).
For the specified load current and power factor, use the generator phasor relation \(\mathbf E_0=\mathbf V+\mathbf I(R_a+jX_s)\) to find the magnitude \(E_0\).
Finally calculate percentage voltage regulation from \((E_0-V)/V\times100\).
ai_sections.caution: OCC and SCC values must correspond to the same field current, and the voltage/current quantities must be used consistently on a per-phase basis. Keep the stated power-factor phasor convention explicit.
ai_sections.key_point: The method is a sequence: OCC + SCC → \(Z_s\) → \(X_s\) → internal emf \(E_0\) → voltage regulation.

ai_sections.title: Synchronous Motor — Principle of Operation
paragraphs: A balanced three-phase stator supply produces a rotating magnetic field at synchronous speed. The rotor carries a magnetic field established by DC excitation.

Electromagnetic torque acts between the rotor field and the rotating stator field. When the rotor field locks with the stator field, the rotor follows it at exactly the same speed in steady synchronous operation.
ai_sections.key_point: The defining idea is magnetic locking: rotor field and stator rotating field move together at synchronous speed.

ai_sections.title: Stepper Motor — Principle and Applications
paragraphs: A stepper motor moves through discrete equal angular steps. The rotor can be moved to, and held at, one of these step positions by controlling the sequence in which stator phase groups are energised.
bullets: In the variable-reluctance example, energising a stator phase makes the rotor teeth align with that magnetic axis to obtain minimum reluctance.
When the next stator phase is energised, the magnetic axis shifts and the rotor advances by one step angle.
The textbook example shows a 30° step, but that value is illustrative rather than universal.
Applications include scanners, printers, 3D printers, plotters, camera lenses, CNC machines, optical/laser actuators and fluid-control systems.

diagrams.title: Cross-sectional view of stepper motor
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.13 · Cross-sectional view of stepper motor · Textbook p. 199

ai_sections.key_point: Sequential excitation converts electrical command pulses into controlled angular position steps.

ai_sections.title: Basic Layout of a Domestic Electrical Installation
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Q9(a) · domestic electrical-installation layout (5M)
paragraphs: In a single-phase domestic installation, the household loads are supplied between phase and neutral at about 230 V. The incoming supply passes through metering, main protection and a distribution board before reaching the final sub-circuits.
derivation: Service wire brings phase and neutral from the supply.
A service fuse in the phase protects the incoming service conductor against over-current.
The energy meter records the electrical energy consumed.
The main MCB controls/protects the entire installation.
The distribution board divides the installation into sub-circuits; each sub-circuit has its own MCB so a fault can be isolated without switching off every circuit.
Metallic enclosures and exposed conductive parts are connected to earth.

diagrams.title: Lay-out of wiring in domestic installations
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.14 · Lay-out of wiring in domestic installations · Textbook p. 201

ai_sections.key_point: Remember the flow: supply → service protection → energy meter → main MCB → distribution board → protected sub-circuits → loads, with earthing of exposed metalwork.

ai_sections.title: Types of Wiring
bullets: Cleat wiring: insulated conductors supported on cleats; simple and mainly suited to temporary work.
Casing-and-capping wiring: conductors run inside a casing that is closed by a cap; neat appearance but requires maintenance.
TRS/CTS batten wiring: tough-rubber/cab-tyre-sheathed cable fixed on wooden battens using clips; neat and resistant to moisture/chemical effects.
Lead/metal-sheathed wiring: insulated conductors protected by a metallic sheath against mechanical and atmospheric damage.
Conduit wiring: conductors are drawn through PVC conduit. It may be surface conduit or concealed conduit; concealed conduit is widely used in domestic/office installations.

diagrams.title: Cleat wiring
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.15 · Cleat wiring · Textbook p. 202

diagrams.title: Conduit wiring
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.18 · Conduit wiring · Textbook p. 203

ai_sections.key_point: For short answers, identify each wiring system by its physical method of supporting/protecting the conductors.

ai_sections.title: Switch Fuse Unit (SFU)
paragraphs: A Switch Fuse Unit is a compact combination of a switch and a fuse, generally enclosed in a metal cover and used at low/medium voltages.
bullets: Switch function: provides switching/isolation of the circuit.
Fuse function: a series fuse element melts under excessive current and interrupts the circuit.
After fuse operation, the fuse element must be replaced before the circuit can be restored.
ai_sections.caution: Verified mismatch: SFU is a switch-and-fuse unit. Do not explain SFU using an earth-leakage/current-balance mechanism; earth-leakage protection belongs under ELCB.
ai_sections.key_point: SFU = switch + fuse: control/isolation plus sacrificial over-current protection.

ai_sections.title: MCB, ELCB and MCCB
pyq_focus: 2024–25 Part A(d) · differentiate MCB and MCCB (2M)
2023–24 Q8(a) · working of MCB (5M)
paragraphs: These three LT protective devices differ mainly in the fault condition they are intended to respond to and the current/fault level of the installation.

rows: Automatically opens for overload and short-circuit conditions; overload tripping uses a bimetal element.
Resettable protection for lower-current final/domestic circuits.
Disconnects supply when an earth-leakage condition indicates an electrical hazard.
Earth-leakage protection; do not treat it as ordinary overload protection.
Protects against overload and short circuit at higher current and fault levels; may have adjustable trip settings.
Used for larger loads, main feeders and industrial distribution.

diagrams.title: MCB
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.24 · MCB · Textbook p. 206

ai_sections.caution: Do not silently substitute RCCB terminology for ELCB unless a supplied source explicitly establishes that equivalence.
ai_sections.key_point: Over-current/short circuit → MCB or MCCB. Earth leakage → ELCB.

ai_sections.title: Earthing — Need, Pipe Earthing and Plate Earthing
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Q9(b) · need and types of earthing (5M)
2024–25 Q8 · pipe earthing (part of 10M)
2023–24 Q8(b) · define earthing and explain types (5M)
paragraphs: Earthing connects the exposed metallic bodies of electrical equipment to earth through a low-resistance conductor and electrode. If a live conductor touches a metal body, the fault current is given a preferred path to ground instead of through a person.
bullets: Need for earthing: reduce electric-shock risk, reduce fire risk due to earth-leakage current, and provide the required neutral/earth reference where applicable.
Pipe earthing: a G.I. pipe about 38 mm in diameter and 2.5 m long is placed vertically in the earth. Charcoal/salt and moisture are used in the illustrated arrangement to keep earth resistance low.
Plate earthing: a G.I. plate of 60 cm × 60 cm × 6 mm is buried in the earth, with charcoal and salt around it and regular watering to maintain low resistance.

ai_sections.key_point: The safety purpose is the same in both methods; the difference is the buried earth electrode: pipe versus plate.

ai_sections.title: Classification of Batteries
paragraphs: A battery converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy and may also be used as a backup source when the main supply is interrupted.

rows: Rechargeable; chemical action can be reversed by charging

ai_sections.key_point: Lead-acid is a secondary (rechargeable) battery.

pyq_focus: 2025–26 Part A(e) · any two advantages of lead-acid battery (2M)
2025–26 Q10 · construction and working of lead-acid battery (part of 10M)
paragraphs: The lead-acid battery is a rechargeable secondary battery used in applications such as automobiles and inverters. The source notes that it can store a high amount of energy and describes it as cheaper and easy to handle, although it is heavy.
bullets: Positive plate: lead dioxide \(PbO_2\).
Negative plate: sponge lead \(Pb\).
Electrolyte: sulphuric acid \(H_2SO_4\) diluted with water in the stated 1:3 proportion.
Separators keep the positive and negative plates electrically apart inside a hard-plastic container.
One cell is about 2.1 V in the construction discussion; a 12 V battery uses six series-connected cells.
Battery rating is expressed in ampere-hours (Ah).

diagrams.title: Lead-acid battery
diagrams.alt: Figure 4.31 · Lead-acid battery · Textbook p. 211

ai_sections.key_point: During discharge both plates tend toward lead sulphate and water is formed; charging reverses the chemical process.

ai_sections.title: Lead-Acid Battery — Electrical Characteristics
pyq_focus: 2023–24 Part A(d) · electrical characteristics of lead-acid battery (2M)
2024–25 Q8(a) · lead-acid battery electrical characteristics (5M)
bullets: Voltage: the fully charged open-circuit cell voltage is stated as about 2.2 V. Terminal voltage falls during discharge and should not be allowed to fall below the stated 1.8 V limit.
Capacity: specified in ampere-hours (Ah). For example, 100 Ah ideally corresponds to 10 A for 10 h, 20 A for 5 h or 40 A for 2.5 h; usable capacity falls as discharge rate increases.
Efficiency: ampere-hour efficiency compares charge delivered during discharge with charge supplied during charging. The source states an Ah-efficiency range of about 90–95%.
Energy (watt-hour) efficiency is lower than ampere-hour efficiency.

formulae.label: Ampere-hour efficiency
formulae.latex: \eta_{Ah}=\dfrac{\text{Ah delivered during discharge}}{\text{Ah absorbed during charge}}\times100

ai_sections.title: UPS — Block Diagram and Operation
pyq_focus: 2025–26 Q10 · UPS operation with block diagram (part of 10M)
paragraphs: An Uninterruptible Power Supply maintains continuity of power for critical AC loads when the normal AC supply is interrupted.
bullets: Block sequence: AC input → rectifier → inverter → filter → critical load.
A battery bank is connected on the DC link between the rectifier and inverter.
Normal supply available: the rectifier converts AC to DC, supplies the inverter and charges the battery.
AC supply fails: the battery supplies DC to the inverter; the inverter converts it back to AC and supplies the load through the filter.
The UPS also helps maintain load-supply quality against input-voltage fluctuations.

diagrams.title: UPS block diagram
diagrams.alt: Figure 5.44 · UPS block diagram · Textbook p. 243

ai_sections.key_point: The inverter feeds the AC load in both conditions; the DC source changes from rectifier to battery when mains power fails.
